params.name: KDE_NPOLE
params.description: Sets the number of motor poles to calculate the correct RPM value

params.name: LAND_SLOPE_RCALC
params.description: This parameter is used when using a rangefinder during landing for altitude correction from baro drift (RNGFND_LANDING=1) and the altitude correction indicates your altitude is lower than the intended slope path. This value is the threshold of the correction to re-calculate the landing approach slope. Set to zero to keep the original slope all the way down and any detected baro drift will be corrected by pitching/throttling up to snap back to resume the original slope path. Otherwise, when a rangefinder altitude correction exceeds this threshold it will trigger a slope re-calculate to give a shallower slope. This also smoothes out the approach when flying over objects such as trees. Recommend a value of 2m.

params.name: LAND_ABORT_DEG
params.description: This parameter is used when using a rangefinder during landing for altitude correction from baro drift (RNGFND_LANDING=1) and the altitude correction indicates your actual altitude is higher than the intended slope path. Normally it would pitch down steeply but that can result in a crash with high airspeed so this allows remembering the baro offset and self-abort the landing and come around for another landing with the correct baro offset applied for a perfect slope. An auto-abort go-around will only happen once, next attempt will not auto-abort again. This operation happens entirely automatically in AUTO mode. This value is the delta degrees threshold to trigger the go-around compared to the original slope. Example: if set to 5 deg and the mission planned slope is 15 deg then if the new slope is 21 then it will go-around. Set to 0 to disable. Requires LAND_SLOPE_RCALC > 0.

params.name: LAND_PITCH_DEG
params.description: Used in autoland to give the minimum pitch in the final stage of landing (after the flare). This parameter can be used to ensure that the final landing attitude is appropriate for the type of undercarriage on the aircraft. Note that it is a minimum pitch only - the landing code will control pitch above this value to try to achieve the configured landing sink rate.

params.name: LAND_FLARE_ALT
params.description: Altitude in autoland at which to lock heading and flare to the LAND_PITCH_DEG pitch. Note that this option is secondary to LAND_FLARE_SEC. For a good landing it preferable that the flare is triggered by LAND_FLARE_SEC.

params.name: LAND_FLARE_SEC
params.description: Vertical time before landing point at which to lock heading and flare with the motor stopped. This is vertical time, and is calculated based solely on the current height above the ground and the current descent rate.  Set to 0 if you only wish to flare based on altitude (see LAND_FLARE_ALT).

params.name: LAND_PF_ALT
params.description: Altitude to trigger pre-flare flight stage where LAND_PF_ARSPD controls airspeed. The pre-flare flight stage trigger works just like LAND_FLARE_ALT but higher. Disabled when LAND_PF_ARSPD is 0.

params.name: LAND_PF_SEC
params.description: Vertical time to ground to trigger pre-flare flight stage where LAND_PF_ARSPD controls airspeed. This pre-flare flight stage trigger works just like LAND_FLARE_SEC but earlier. Disabled when LAND_PF_ARSPD is 0.

params.name: LAND_PF_ARSPD
params.description: Desired airspeed during pre-flare flight stage. This is useful to reduce airspeed just before the flare. Use 0 to disable.

params.name: LAND_THR_SLEW
params.description: This parameter sets the slew rate for the throttle during auto landing. When this is zero the THR_SLEWRATE parameter is used during landing. The value is a percentage throttle change per second, so a value of 20 means to advance the throttle over 5 seconds on landing. Values below 50 are not recommended as it may cause a stall when airspeed is low and you can not throttle up fast enough.

params.name: LAND_DISARMDELAY
params.description: After a landing has completed using a LAND waypoint, automatically disarm after this many seconds have passed. Use 0 to not disarm.

params.name: LAND_THEN_NEUTRL
params.humanName: Set servos to neutral after landing
params.description: When enabled, after an autoland and auto-disarm via LAND_DISARMDELAY happens then set all servos to neutral. This is helpful when an aircraft has a rough landing upside down or a crazy angle causing the servos to strain.

params.name: LAND_ABORT_THR
params.description: Allow a landing abort to trigger with an input throttle >= 90%. This works with or without stick-mixing enabled.

params.name: LAND_FLAP_PERCNT
params.description: The amount of flaps (as a percentage) to apply in the landing approach and flare of an automatic landing

params.name: LAND_OPTIONS
params.description: Bitmask of options to use with landing.

bitmask.label: honor min throttle during landing flare
Increase Target landing airspeed constraint From Trim Airspeed to AIRSPEED_MAX

params.name: LAND_FLARE_AIM
params.description: This parameter controls how much the aim point is moved to allow for the time spent in the flare manoeuvre. When set to 100% the aim point is adjusted on the assumption that the flare sink rate controller instantly achieves the sink rate set by TECS_LAND_SINK. when set to 0%, no aim point adjustment is made. If the plane consistently touches down short of the aim point reduce the parameter and vice verse.

params.name: LAND_WIND_COMP
params.description: This param controls how much headwind compensation is used when landing.  Headwind speed component multiplied by this parameter is added to TECS_LAND_ARSPD command.  Set to Zero to disable.  Note:  The target landing airspeed command is still limited to AIRSPEED_MAX.

params.name: LGR_ENABLE
params.description: Enable landing gear control

params.name: LGR_STARTUP
params.description: Landing Gear Startup behaviour control

params.name: LGR_DEPLOY_PIN
params.description: Pin number to use for detection of gear deployment. If set to -1 feedback is disabled. Some common values are given, but see the Wiki's "GPIOs" page for how to determine the pin number for a given autopilot.

params.name: LGR_DEPLOY_POL
params.description: Polarity for feedback pin. If this is 1 then the pin should be high when gear are deployed. If set to 0 then then deployed gear level is low.

params.name: LGR_WOW_PIN
params.description: Pin number to use for feedback of weight on wheels condition. If set to -1 feedback is disabled. Some common values are given, but see the Wiki's "GPIOs" page for how to determine the pin number for a given autopilot.

params.name: LGR_WOW_POL
params.humanName: Weight on wheels feedback pin polarity
params.description: Polarity for feedback pin. If this is 1 then the pin should be high when there is weight on wheels. If set to 0 then then weight on wheels level is low.

params.name: LGR_DEPLOY_ALT
params.description: Altitude where the landing gear will be deployed. This should be lower than the RETRACT_ALT. If zero then altitude is not used for deploying landing gear. Only applies when vehicle is armed.

params.name: LGR_RETRACT_ALT
params.description: Altitude where the landing gear will be retracted. This should be higher than the DEPLOY_ALT. If zero then altitude is not used for retracting landing gear. Only applies when vehicle is armed.

params.name: LGR_OPTIONS
params.description: Options to retract or deploy landing gear in Auto, Takeoff and Autoland modes

params.name: LOG_BACKEND_TYPE
params.description: Bitmap of what Logger backend types to enable. Block-based logging is available on SITL and boards with dataflash chips. Multiple backends can be selected.

params.name: LOG_FILE_BUFSIZE
params.humanName: Logging File and Block Backend buffer size max (in kibibytes)
params.description: The File and Block backends use a buffer to store data before writing to the block device.  Raising this value may reduce "gaps" in your SD card logging but increases memory usage.  This buffer size may be reduced to free up available memory

params.name: LOG_DISARMED
params.description: If LOG_DISARMED is set to 1 then logging will be enabled at all times including when disarmed. Logging before arming can make for very large logfiles but can help a lot when tracking down startup issues and is necessary if logging of EKF replay data is selected via the LOG_REPLAY parameter. If LOG_DISARMED is set to 2, then logging will be enabled when disarmed, but not if a USB connection is detected. This can be used to prevent unwanted data logs being generated when the vehicle is connected via USB for log downloading or parameter changes. If LOG_DISARMED is set to 3 then logging will happen while disarmed, but if the vehicle never arms then the logs using the filesystem backend will be discarded on the next boot.

values.label: Discard log on reboot if never armed

params.name: LOG_REPLAY
params.humanName: Enable logging of information needed for Replay
params.description: If LOG_REPLAY is set to 1 then the EKF2 and EKF3 state estimators will log detailed information needed for diagnosing problems with the Kalman filter. LOG_DISARMED must be set to 1 or 2 or else the log will not contain the pre-flight data required for replay testing of the EKF's. It is suggested that you also raise LOG_FILE_BUFSIZE to give more buffer space for logging and use a high quality microSD card to ensure no sensor data is lost.

params.name: LOG_FILE_DSRMROT
params.humanName: Stop logging to current file on disarm
params.description: When set, the current log file is closed when the vehicle is disarmed.  If LOG_DISARMED is set then a fresh log will be opened. Applies to the File and Block logging backends.

params.name: LOG_MAV_BUFSIZE
params.humanName: Maximum AP_Logger MAVLink Backend buffer size
params.description: Maximum amount of memory to allocate to AP_Logger-over-mavlink

params.name: LOG_FILE_TIMEOUT
params.humanName: Timeout before giving up on file writes
params.description: This controls the amount of time before failing writes to a log file cause the file to be closed and logging stopped.

params.name: LOG_FILE_MB_FREE
params.humanName: Old logs on the SD card will be deleted to maintain this amount of free space
params.description: Set this such that the free space is larger than your largest typical flight log

params.name: LOG_FILE_RATEMAX
params.humanName: Maximum logging rate for file backend
params.description: This sets the maximum rate that streaming log messages will be logged to the file backend. A value of zero means that rate limiting is disabled.

params.name: LOG_MAV_RATEMAX
params.humanName: Maximum logging rate for mavlink backend
params.description: This sets the maximum rate that streaming log messages will be logged to the mavlink backend. A value of zero means that rate limiting is disabled.

params.name: LOG_BLK_RATEMAX
params.humanName: Maximum logging rate for block backend
params.description: This sets the maximum rate that streaming log messages will be logged to the block backend. A value of zero means that rate limiting is disabled.

params.name: LOG_DARM_RATEMAX
params.description: This sets the maximum rate that streaming log messages will be logged to any backend when disarmed. A value of zero means that the normal backend rate limit is applied.

params.name: LOG_MAX_FILES
params.description: This sets the maximum number of log file that will be written on dataflash or sd card before starting to rotate log number. Limit is capped at 500 logs.

params.name: MAV_SYSID
params.humanName: MAVLink system ID of this vehicle
params.description: Allows setting an individual MAVLink system id for this vehicle to distinguish it from others on the same network.

params.name: MAV_GCS_SYSID
params.description: This sets what MAVLink source system IDs are accepted for GCS failsafe handling, RC overrides and manual control. When MAV_GCS_SYSID_HI is less than MAV_GCS_SYSID then only this value is considered to be a GCS. When MAV_GCS_SYSID_HI is greater than or equal to MAV_GCS_SYSID then the range of values between MAV_GCS_SYSID and MAV_GCS_SYSID_HI (inclusive) are all treated as valid GCS MAVLink system IDs

params.name: MAV_GCS_SYSID_HI
params.description: Upper limit of MAVLink source system IDs considered to be from the GCS. When this is less than MAV_GCS_SYSID then only MAV_GCS_SYSID is used as GCS ID. When this is greater than or equal to MAV_GCS_SYSID then the range of values from MAV_GCS_SYSID to MAV_GCS_SYSID_HI (inclusive) is treated as a GCS ID.

params.description: Used for average cell voltage calculation

params.name: MSP_OPTIONS
params.description: A bitmask to set some MSP specific options: EnableTelemetryMode-allows "push" mode telemetry when only rx line of OSD ic connected to autopilot,  EnableBTFLFonts-uses indexes corresponding to Betaflight fonts if OSD uses those instead of ArduPilot fonts. EnableINAVFonts uses INAV fonts and overrides EnableBTFLFonts if that option is enabled. ForceVTXHighPower always reports the vehicle as armed so a VTX that drops to low power when disarmed stays at full power.

params.name: NAVL1_PERIOD
params.description: Period in seconds of L1 tracking loop. This parameter is the primary control for aggressiveness of turns in auto mode. This needs to be larger for less responsive airframes. The default is quite conservative, but for most RC aircraft will lead to reasonable flight. For smaller more agile aircraft a value closer to 15 is appropriate, or even as low as 10 for some very agile aircraft. When tuning, change this value in small increments, as a value that is much too small (say 5 or 10 below the right value) can lead to very radical turns, and a risk of stalling.

params.name: NAVL1_DAMPING
params.description: Damping ratio for L1 control. Increase this in increments of 0.05 if you are getting overshoot in path tracking. You should not need a value below 0.7 or above 0.85.

params.name: NAVL1_XTRACK_I
params.description: Crosstrack error integrator gain. This gain is applied to the crosstrack error to ensure it converges to zero. Set to zero to disable. Smaller values converge slower, higher values will cause crosstrack error oscillation.

params.name: NAVL1_LIM_BANK
params.description: The sealevel bank angle limit for a continuous loiter. (Used to calculate airframe loading limits at higher altitudes). Setting to 0, will instead just scale the loiter radius directly

params.name: PLND_ENABLED
params.description: Precision Land enabled/disabled

params.name: PLND_TYPE
params.description: Precision Land Type

params.name: PLND_YAW_ALIGN
params.description: Yaw angle from body x-axis to sensor x-axis.

params.name: PLND_LAND_OFS_X
params.description: Desired landing position of the camera forward of the target in vehicle body frame

params.name: PLND_LAND_OFS_Y
params.description: desired landing position of the camera right of the target in vehicle body frame

params.name: PLND_EST_TYPE
params.description: Specifies the estimation method to be used

params.name: PLND_ACC_P_NSE
params.description: Kalman Filter Accelerometer Noise, higher values weight the input from the camera more, accels less

params.name: PLND_CAM_POS_X
params.description: X position of the camera in body frame. Positive X is forward of the origin.

params.name: PLND_CAM_POS_Y
params.description: Y position of the camera in body frame. Positive Y is to the right of the origin.

params.name: PLND_CAM_POS_Z
params.description: Z position of the camera in body frame. Positive Z is down from the origin.

params.name: PLND_BUS
params.description: Precland sensor bus for I2C sensors.

params.name: PLND_LAG
params.description: Precision Landing sensor lag, to cope with variable landing_target latency

params.name: PLND_XY_DIST_MAX
params.humanName: Precision Landing maximum distance to target before descending
params.description: The vehicle will not start descending if the landing target is detected and it is further than this many meters away. Set 0 to always descend.

params.name: PLND_STRICT
params.description: How strictly should the vehicle land on the target if target is lost

params.name: PLND_RET_MAX
params.humanName: PrecLand Maximum number of retires for a failed landing
params.description: PrecLand Maximum number of retires for a failed landing. Set to zero to disable landing retry.

params.name: PLND_TIMEOUT
params.description: Time for which vehicle continues descend even if target is lost. After this time period, vehicle will attempt a landing retry depending on PLND_STRICT parameter.

params.name: PLND_RET_BEHAVE
params.description: Prec Land will do the action selected by this parameter if a retry to a landing is needed

values.label: Go to the last location where landing target was detected
Go towards the approximate location of the detected landing target

params.name: PLND_ALT_MIN
params.description: Vehicle will continue landing vertically even if target is lost below this height. This needs a rangefinder to work. Set to zero to disable this.

params.name: PLND_ALT_MAX
params.description: Vehicle will continue landing vertically until this height if target is not found. Below this height if landing target is not found, landing retry/failsafe might be attempted. This needs a rangefinder to work. Set to zero to disable this.

params.name: PLND_OPTIONS
params.description: Precision Landing Extra Options

bitmask.label: Allow Precision Landing after manual reposition
Maintain high speed in final descent

params.name: PTCH2SRV_TCONST
params.description: Time constant in seconds from demanded to achieved pitch angle. Most models respond well to 0.5. May be reduced for faster responses, but setting lower than a model can achieve will not help.

params.name: PTCH2SRV_RMAX_UP
params.description: This sets the maximum nose up pitch rate that the attitude controller will demand (degrees/sec) in angle stabilized modes. Setting it to zero disables the limit.

params.name: PTCH2SRV_RMAX_DN
params.description: This sets the maximum nose down pitch rate that the attitude controller will demand (degrees/sec) in angle stabilized modes. Setting it to zero disables the limit.

params.name: PTCH2SRV_RLL
params.description: Gain added to pitch to keep aircraft from descending or ascending in turns. Increase in increments of 0.05 to reduce altitude loss. Decrease for altitude gain.

params.name: PTCH_RATE_P
params.humanName: Pitch axis rate controller P gain
params.description: Pitch axis rate controller P gain. Corrects in proportion to the difference between the desired pitch rate vs actual pitch rate

params.name: PTCH_RATE_I
params.humanName: Pitch axis rate controller I gain
params.description: Pitch axis rate controller I gain.  Corrects long-term difference in desired pitch rate vs actual pitch rate

params.name: PTCH_RATE_IMAX
params.humanName: Pitch axis rate controller I gain maximum
params.description: Pitch axis rate controller I gain maximum.  Constrains the maximum that the I term will output

params.name: PTCH_RATE_D
params.humanName: Pitch axis rate controller D gain
params.description: Pitch axis rate controller D gain.  Compensates for short-term change in desired pitch rate vs actual pitch rate

params.name: PTCH_RATE_FF
params.humanName: Pitch axis rate controller feed forward
params.description: Pitch axis rate controller feed forward

params.name: PTCH_RATE_FLTT
params.humanName: Pitch axis rate controller target frequency in Hz
params.description: Pitch axis rate controller target frequency in Hz

params.name: PTCH_RATE_FLTE
params.humanName: Pitch axis rate controller error frequency in Hz
params.description: Pitch axis rate controller error frequency in Hz

params.name: PTCH_RATE_FLTD
params.humanName: Pitch axis rate controller derivative frequency in Hz
params.description: Pitch axis rate controller derivative frequency in Hz

params.name: PTCH_RATE_SMAX
params.description: Sets an upper limit on the slew rate produced by the combined P and D gains. If the amplitude of the control action produced by the rate feedback exceeds this value, then the D+P gain is reduced to respect the limit. This limits the amplitude of high frequency oscillations caused by an excessive gain. The limit should be set to no more than 25% of the actuators maximum slew rate to allow for load effects. Note: The gain will not be reduced to less than 10% of the nominal value. A value of zero will disable this feature.

params.name: PTCH_RATE_PDMX
params.humanName: Pitch axis rate controller PD sum maximum
params.description: Pitch axis rate controller PD sum maximum.  The maximum/minimum value that the sum of the P and D term can output

params.name: PTCH_RATE_D_FF
params.description: FF D Gain which produces an output that is proportional to the rate of change of the target

params.name: PTCH_RATE_NTF
params.description: Pitch Target notch filter index

params.name: PTCH_RATE_NEF
params.description: Pitch Error notch filter index

params.name: PTCH2SRV_ACCEL
params.description: Pitch acceleration limit. Setting to zero disables input shaping.

params.name: PTCH_ANGLE_P
params.description: Pitch angle P gain. If zero a gain of (1 / PTCH2SRV_TCONST) will be used.

params.name: PUP_ENABLE
params.description: Enable pullup after altitude wait

params.name: PUP_ELEV_OFS
params.humanName: Elevator deflection used before starting pullup
params.description: Elevator deflection offset from -1 to 1 while waiting for airspeed to rise before starting close loop control of the pullup.

params.name: PUP_NG_LIM
params.humanName: Maximum normal load factor during pullup
params.description: This is the nominal maximum value of normal load factor used during the closed loop pitch rate control of the pullup.

params.name: PUP_NG_JERK_LIM
params.humanName: Maximum normal load factor rate of change during pullup
params.description: The normal load factor used for closed loop pitch rate control of the pullup will be ramped up to the value set by PUP_NG_LIM at the rate of change set by this parameter. The parameter value specified will be scaled internally by 1/EAS2TAS.

params.name: PUP_PITCH
params.description: The vehicle will attempt achieve this pitch angle during the pull-up maneouvre.

params.name: PUP_ARSPD_START
params.description: Target airspeed for initial airspeed wait

params.name: PUP_PITCH_START
params.description: Target pitch for initial pullup

params.name: QWIK_ENABLE
params.description: Enable quicktune system

params.name: QWIK_AXES
params.description: Axes to tune

params.name: QWIK_DOUBLE_TIME
params.description: Time to double a tuning parameter. Raise this for a slower tune.

params.name: QWIK_GAIN_MARGIN
params.description: Reduction in gain after oscillation detected. Raise this number to get a more conservative tune

params.name: QWIK_OSC_SMAX
params.description: Threshold for oscillation detection. A lower value will lead to a more conservative tune.

params.name: QWIK_YAW_P_MAX
params.description: Maximum value for yaw P gain

params.name: QWIK_YAW_D_MAX
params.description: Maximum value for yaw D gain

params.name: QWIK_RP_PI_RATIO
params.description: Ratio between P and I gains for roll and pitch. Raise this to get a lower I gain

params.name: QWIK_Y_PI_RATIO
params.description: Ratio between P and I gains for yaw. Raise this to get a lower I gain

params.name: QWIK_AUTO_FILTER
params.description: When enabled the PID filter settings are automatically set based on INS_GYRO_FILTER

params.name: QWIK_AUTO_SAVE
params.description: Number of seconds after completion of tune to auto-save. This is useful when using a 2 position switch for quicktune. Zero (the default value) disables automatic saving, and you will need to have a 3 position switch to save or use GCS auxilliary functions.

params.name: QWIK_REDUCE_MAX
params.description: This controls how much quicktune is allowed to lower gains from the original gains. If the vehicle already has a reasonable tune and is not oscillating then you can set this to zero to prevent gain reductions. The default of 20% is reasonable for most vehicles. Using a maximum gain reduction lowers the chance of an angle P oscillation happening if quicktune gets a false positive oscillation at a low gain, which can result in very low rate gains and a dangerous angle P oscillation.

params.name: QWIK_OPTIONS
params.description: Additional options. When the Two Position Switch option is enabled then a high switch position will start the tune, low will disable the tune. you should also set a QUIK_AUTO_SAVE time so that you will be able to save the tune.

params.name: QWIK_ANGLE_MAX
params.humanName: maximum angle error for tune abort
params.description: If while tuning the angle error goes over this limit then the tune will aborts to prevent a bad oscillation in the case of the tuning algorithm failing. If you get an error "Quicktune: attitude error ABORTING" and you think it is a false positive then you can either raise this parameter or you can try increasing the QWIK_DOUBLE_TIME to do the tune more slowly.

params.name: Q_ENABLE
params.description: This enables QuadPlane functionality, assuming multicopter motors start on output 5. If this is set to 2 then when starting AUTO mode it will initially be in VTOL AUTO mode.

params.name: Q_TRANSITION_MS
params.description: Transition time in milliseconds after minimum airspeed is reached

params.name: Q_PILOT_SPD_UP
params.description: The maximum ascending vertical velocity the pilot may request in m/s

params.name: Q_PILOT_SPD_DN
params.description: The maximum vertical velocity the pilot may request in m/s going down. If 0, uses Q_PILOT_SPD_UP value.

params.name: Q_PILOT_ACCEL_Z
params.description: The vertical acceleration used when pilot is controlling the altitude

params.name: Q_RC_SPEED
params.description: This is the PWM refresh rate in Hz for QuadPlane quad motors

params.name: Q_ASSIST_SPEED
params.description: This is the speed below which the quad motors will provide stability and lift assistance in fixed wing modes. The default value of 0 disables assistance but will generate a pre-arm failure to encourage users to set this parameter to -1, or a positive, non-zero value. If this is set to -1 then all Q_ASSIST features are disabled except during transitions. A high non-zero,positive value will lead to more false positives which can waste battery. A lower value will result in less false positive, but will result in assistance taking longer to trigger. If unsure then set to 3 m/s below the minimum airspeed you will fly at. If you don't have an airspeed sensor then use 5 m/s below the minimum airspeed you fly at.

params.name: Q_YAW_RATE_MAX
params.description: This is the maximum yaw rate for pilot input on rudder stick in degrees/second and weathervaning is limited to half of this value

params.name: Q_LAND_FINAL_SPD
params.description: The descent speed for the final stage of landing in m/s

params.name: Q_LAND_FINAL_ALT
params.description: The altitude at which we should switch to Q_LAND_FINAL_SPD descent rate

params.name: Q_TRAN_PIT_MAX
params.description: Maximum pitch during transition to auto fixed wing flight

params.name: Q_FRAME_CLASS
params.description: Controls major frame class for multicopter component

params.name: Q_FRAME_TYPE
params.description: Controls motor mixing for multicopter component

params.name: Q_VFWD_GAIN
params.description: The use of this parameter is no longer recommended and has been superseded by a method that works in all VTOL modes with the exception of QAUTOTUNE which is controlled by the Q_FWD_THR_USE parameter. This Q_VFD_GAIN parameter controls use of the forward motor in VTOL modes that use the velocity controller. Set to 0 to disable this function. A value of 0.05 is a good place to start if you want to use the forward motor for position control. No forward motor will be used in QSTABILIZE or QHOVER modes. Use with QLOITER for position hold with the forward motor.

params.name: Q_RTL_ALT
params.description: The altitude which QRTL mode heads to initially

params.name: Q_RTL_MODE
params.description: If this is set to 1 then an RTL will change to QRTL when within RTL_RADIUS meters of the RTL destination, VTOL approach: vehicle will RTL at RTL alt and circle with a radius of Q_FW_LND_APR_RAD down to Q_RTL_ALT and then transition into the wind and QRTL, see 'AUTO VTOL Landing', QRTL Always: do a QRTL instead of RTL

params.name: Q_GUIDED_MODE
params.description: This enables use of VTOL in guided mode. When enabled the aircraft will switch to VTOL flight when the guided destination is reached and hover at the destination.

params.name: Q_ESC_CAL
params.description: This is used to calibrate the throttle range of the VTOL motors. Please read https://ardupilot.org/plane/docs/quadplane-esc-calibration.html before using. This parameter is automatically set back to 0 on every boot. This parameter only takes effect in QSTABILIZE mode. When set to 1 the output of all motors will come directly from the throttle stick when armed, and will be zero when disarmed. When set to 2 the output of all motors will be maximum when armed and zero when disarmed. Make sure you remove all properllers before using.

params.name: Q_VFWD_ALT
params.description: Controls altitude to disable forward velocity assist when below this relative altitude. This is useful to keep the forward velocity propeller from hitting the ground. Rangefinder height data is incorporated when available.

params.name: Q_LAND_ICE_CUT
params.description: This controls stopping an internal combustion engine in the final landing stage of a VTOL. This is important for aircraft where the forward thrust engine may experience prop-strike if left running during landing. This requires the engine controls are enabled using the ICE_* parameters.

params.name: Q_ASSIST_ANGLE
params.description: This is the angular error in attitude beyond which the quadplane VTOL motors will provide stability assistance. This will only be used if Q_ASSIST_SPEED is also positive and non-zero. Assistance will be given if the attitude is outside the normal attitude limits by at least 5 degrees and the angular error in roll or pitch is greater than this angle for at least Q_ASSIST_DELAY seconds. Set to zero to disable angle assistance.

params.name: Q_ASSIST_OPTIONS
params.description: Options for special QAssist features

bitmask.label: Disable force fixed wing controller recovery

params.name: Q_MAV_TYPE
params.description: This controls the mavlink type given in HEARTBEAT messages. For some GCS types a particular setting will be needed for correct operation.

params.name: Q_OPTIONS
params.description: See description for each bitmask bit description

bitmask.label: Level Transition-keep wings within LEVEL_ROLL_LIMIT and only use forward motor(s) for climb during transition
Allow FW Takeoff-if bit is not set then NAV_TAKEOFF command on quadplanes will instead perform a NAV_VTOL takeoff
Allow FW Land-if bit is not set then NAV_LAND command on quadplanes will instead perform a NAV_VTOL_LAND
Vtol Takeoff Frame-command NAV_VTOL_TAKEOFF alt set by the command's reference frame not above current location
Always use FW spiral approach-always use Use a fixed wing spiral approach for VTOL landings
USE QRTL-instead of QLAND for rc failsafe when in VTOL modes
Use Governor-use ICE Idle Governor in MANUAL for forward motor
Mtrs_Only_Qassist-in tailsitters only uses VTOL motors and not flying surfaces for QASSIST
Disarmed Yaw Tilt-enable motor tilt for yaw when disarmed
Delay Spoolup-delay VTOL spoolup for 2 seconds after arming
Disable speed based Qassist when using synthetic airspeed estimates
Disable Ground Effect Compensation-on baro altitude reports
Ignore forward flight angle limits-in Qmodes and use Q_A_ANGLE_MAX exclusively
ThrLandControl-enable throttle stick control of landing rate
DisableApproach-disable use of approach and airbrake stages in VTOL landing
EnableLandResposition-enable pilot controlled repositioning in AUTO land.Descent will pause while repositioning
ARMVTOL-arm only in VTOL modes (or AUTO mode when current nav cmd is VTOL Takeoff)
CompleteTransition-to fixed wing if Q_TRANS_FAIL timer times out instead of QLAND
Force RTL mode-forces RTL mode on rc failsafe in VTOL modes overriding bit 5(USE_QRTL)
Tilt rotor-tilt motors up when disarmed in FW modes (except manual) to prevent ground strikes.
Scale FF by the ratio of VTOL to plane angle P gains in Position 1 phase of transition into VTOL flight as well as reducing VTOL angle P based on airspeed.

params.name: Q_TRANS_DECEL
params.description: This is deceleration rate that will be used in calculating the stopping distance when transitioning from fixed wing flight to multicopter flight.

params.name: Q_TRIM_PITCH
params.description: This sets the compensation for the pitch angle trim difference between calibrated AHRS level and vertical flight pitch. NOTE! this is relative to calibrated AHRS trim, not forward flight trim which includes PTCH_TRIM_DEG. For tailsitters, this is relative to a baseline of 90 degrees in AHRS.

params.name: Q_FW_LND_APR_RAD
params.humanName: Quadplane fixed wing landing approach radius
params.description: This provides the radius used, when using a fixed wing landing approach. If set to 0 then the WP_LOITER_RAD will be selected.

params.name: Q_TRANS_FAIL
params.description: Maximum time allowed for forward transitions, exceeding this time will cancel the transition and the aircraft will immediately change to the mode set by Q_TRANS_FAIL_ACT or finish the transition depending on Q_OPTIONS bit 19. 0 for no limit.

params.name: Q_THROTTLE_EXPO
params.description: Amount of curvature in throttle curve: 0 is linear, 1 is cubic

params.name: Q_ACRO_RLL_RATE
params.description: The maximum roll rate at full stick deflection in QACRO mode

params.name: Q_ACRO_PIT_RATE
params.description: The maximum pitch rate at full stick deflection in QACRO mode

params.name: Q_ACRO_YAW_RATE
params.description: The maximum yaw rate at full stick deflection in QACRO mode

params.name: Q_TKOFF_FAIL_SCL
params.description: Scalar for how long past the expected takeoff time a takeoff should be considered as failed and the vehicle will switch to QLAND. If set to 0 there is no limit on takeoff time.

params.name: Q_TKOFF_ARSP_LIM
params.description: Airspeed limit during takeoff. If the airspeed exceeds this level the vehicle will switch to QLAND. This is useful for ensuring that you don't takeoff into excessively strong wind. If set to 0 there is no limit on airspeed during takeoff.

params.name: Q_ASSIST_ALT
params.description: This is the altitude below which quadplane assistance will be triggered. This acts the same way as Q_ASSIST_ANGLE and Q_ASSIST_SPEED, but triggers if the aircraft drops below the given altitude while the VTOL motors are not running. A value of zero disables this feature. The altitude is calculated as being above ground level. The height above ground is given from a Lidar used if available and RNGFND_LANDING=1. Otherwise it comes from terrain data if TERRAIN_FOLLOW=1 and comes from height above home otherwise.

params.name: Q_ASSIST_DELAY
params.description: This is delay between the assistance thresholds being met and the assistance starting.

params.name: Q_FWD_MANTHR_MAX
params.humanName: VTOL manual forward throttle max percent
params.description: Maximum value for manual forward throttle; used with RC option FWD_THR (209)

params.name: Q_BACKTRANS_MS
params.humanName: SLT and Tiltrotor back transition pitch limit duration
params.description: Pitch angle will increase from 0 to angle max over this duration when switching into VTOL flight in a position control mode. 0 Disables.

params.name: Q_TRANS_FAIL_ACT
params.description: This sets the mode that is changed to when Q_TRANS_FAIL time elapses, if set. See also Q_OPTIONS bit 19: CompleteTransition if Q_TRANS_FAIL

params.name: Q_LAND_ALTCHG
params.description: The maximum altitude change allowed during land detection. You can raise this value if you find that landing detection takes a long time to complete. It is the maximum change in altitude over a period of 4 seconds for landing to be detected

params.name: Q_NAVALT_MIN
params.description: This is the altitude in meters above which navigation begins in auto takeoff. Below this altitude the target roll and pitch will be zero. A value of zero disables the feature

params.name: Q_PLT_Y_RATE
params.description: Pilot controlled yaw rate max. Used in all pilot controlled modes except QAcro

params.name: Q_PLT_Y_EXPO
params.description: Pilot controlled yaw expo to allow faster rotation when stick at edges

params.name: Q_PLT_Y_RATE_TC
params.humanName: Pilot yaw rate control input time constant
params.description: Pilot yaw rate control input time constant. Low numbers lead to sharper response, higher numbers to softer response.

params.name: Q_RTL_ALT_MIN
params.description: If VTOL motors are active QRTL mode will VTOL climb to at least this altitude before returning home. If outside 150% the larger of WP_LOITER_RAD and RTL_RADIUS the vehicle will VTOL climb to Q_RTL_ALT. This parameter has no effect if the vehicle is in forward flight. Should be between Q_LAND_FINAL_ALT and Q_RTL_ALT

params.name: Q_FWD_THR_GAIN
params.description: This parameter sets the gain from forward accel/tilt to forward throttle in certain Q modes. The Q modes this feature operates in is controlled by the Q_FWD_THR_USE parameter. Vehicles using separate forward thrust motors, eg quadplanes, should set this parameter to (all up weight) / (maximum combined thrust of forward motors) with a value of 2 being typical. Vehicles that tilt lifting rotors to provide forward thrust should set this parameter to (all up weight) / (weight lifted by tilting rotors) which for most aircraft can be approximated as (total number of lifting rotors) / (number of lifting rotors that tilt). When using this method of forward throttle control, the forward tilt angle limit is controlled by the Q_FWD_PIT_LIM parameter.

params.name: Q_FWD_PIT_LIM
params.description: When forward throttle is being controlled by the Q_FWD_THR_GAIN parameter in Q modes, the vehicle forward (nose down) pitch rotation will be limited to the value specified by this parameter and the any additional forward acceleration required will be produced by use of the forward thrust motor(s) or tilting of moveable rotors. Larger values allow the vehicle to pitch more nose down. Set initially to the amount of nose down pitch required to remove wing lift.

params.name: Q_FWD_THR_USE
params.description: This parameter determines when the feature that uses forward throttle instead of forward tilt is used. The amount of forward throttle is controlled by the Q_FWD_THR_GAIN parameter. The maximum amount of forward pitch allowed is controlled by the Q_FWD_PIT_LIM parameter. Q_FWD_THR_USE = 0 disables the feature. Q_FWD_THR_USE = 1 enables the feature in all position controlled modes such as QLOITER, QLAND, QRTL and VTOL TAKEOFF. Q_FWD_THR_USE = 2 enables the feature in all Q modes except QAUTOTUNE and QACRO. When enabling the feature, the legacy method of controlling forward throttle use via velocity controller error should be disabled by setting Q_VFWD_GAIN to 0. Do not use this feature with tailsitters.

values.label: On in all position controlled Q modes
On in all Q modes except QAUTOTUNE and QACRO

params.name: Q_BCK_PIT_LIM
params.description: This sets the maximum number of degrees of back or pitch up in Q modes when the airspeed is at AIRSPEED_MIN, and is used to prevent excessive sutructural loads when pitching up decelerate. If airspeed is above or below AIRSPEED_MIN, the pitch up/back will be adjusted according to the formula pitch_limit = Q_BCK_PIT_LIM * (AIRSPEED_MIN / IAS)^2. The backwards/up pitch limit controlled by this parameter is in addition to limiting applied by PTCH_LIM_MAX_DEG and Q_A_ANGLE_MAX. The BCK_PIT_LIM limit is only applied when Q_FWD_THR_USE is set to 1 or 2 and the vehicle is flying in a mode that uses forward throttle instead of forward tilt to generate forward speed. Set to a non positive value 0 to deactivate this limit.

params.name: Q_APPROACH_DIST
params.description: The minimum distance from the destination to use the fixed wing airbrake and approach code for landing approach. This is useful if you don't want the fixed wing approach logic to be used when you are close to the destination. Set to zero to always use fixed wing approach.

params.name: Q_TKOFF_RPM_MIN
params.description: Auto takeoff (in Auto or Guided) is not permitted until motors report at least this RPM. Set to zero to disable check (which also disables Q_TKOFF_RPM_MAX).

params.name: Q_TKOFF_RPM_MAX
params.description: Auto takeoff (in Auto or Guided) is not permitted until motors report no more than this RPM. Set to zero to disable check. Q_TKOFF_RPM_MIN must also be set to a non-zero value to enable this check.

params.name: Q_THRST_LOSS_OPT
params.description: Configuration for thrust loss detection detection, this results in "Potential VTOL Thrust Loss" warnings. This detection also allows the motor mixer to ignore the failed motor allowing better use of the remaining motors.

bitmask.label: Disable thrust loss detection in transtions and fixed wing modes. Thrust loss detection will only run in VTOL modes.

params.name: Q_AUTOTUNE_AGGR

params.name: Q_AUTOTUNE_MIN_D

params.name: Q_AUTOTUNE_GMBK
params.description: Fraction by which tuned P and D gains are reduced after rate and angle AutoTune steps complete. This provides extra stability margin by reducing gains slightly from the optimal values found during tuning. A value of 0.0 applies no reduction. A value of 0.25 reduces tuned gains by 25%.

params.name: Q_M_BAT_VOLT_MIN

params.name: Q_M_BAT_CURR_MAX

params.name: Q_M_PWM_MIN

params.name: Q_M_PWM_MAX

params.name: Q_M_SPIN_ARM

params.name: Q_M_BAT_CURR_TC

params.name: Q_M_SPOOL_TIME

A higher scaling factor will put more of the load on the booster motor. A value of 1 will set the BoostThrottle equal to the main throttle.

params.name: Q_M_SAFE_TIME
params.humanName: PWM re-enable delay after arming when disarmed pwm was disabled
params.description: Delay after arming before spool transitions are allowed, used to let ESCs/servos complete startup when PWM was disabled while disarmed.

params.name: Q_M_OPTIONS
params.description: Motor options

params.name: Q_M_SPOOL_TIM_DN
params.description: Time to ramp the throttle ceiling down toward zero. If 0, SPOOL_TIME is used.

params.name: Q_M_IDLE_SEC
params.description: Delay after reaching ground idle when armed to allow ESC startup to complete.

params.name: Q_P_D_POS_P
params.description: Position (vertical) controller P gain. Converts the difference between the desired altitude and actual altitude into a climb or descent rate which is passed to the throttle rate controller. Previously _POSZ_P.

params.name: Q_P_NE_POS_P
params.description: Position controller P gain. Converts the distance (in the latitude direction) to the target location into a desired speed which is then passed to the loiter latitude rate controller. Previously _POSXY_P.

params.name: Q_P_ANGLE_MAX
params.description: Maximum lean angle autopilot can request. Set to zero to use ANGLE_MAX parameter value

params.name: Q_P_NE_JERK
params.humanName: Jerk limit for the horizontal kinematic input shaping
params.description: Jerk limit of the horizontal kinematic path generation used to determine how quickly the aircraft varies the acceleration target

params.name: Q_P_D_JERK
params.humanName: Jerk limit for the vertical kinematic input shaping
params.description: Jerk limit of the vertical kinematic path generation used to determine how quickly the aircraft varies the acceleration target

params.name: Q_P_D_VEL_P
params.description: Velocity (vertical) controller P gain. Converts the difference between desired vertical speed and actual speed into a desired acceleration that is passed to the throttle acceleration controller. Previously _VELZ_P.

params.name: Q_P_D_VEL_I
params.description: Velocity (vertical) controller I gain. Corrects long-term difference in desired velocity to a target acceleration. Previously _VELZ_I.

params.name: Q_P_D_VEL_IMAX
params.description: Velocity (vertical) controller I gain maximum. Constrains the target acceleration that the I gain will output. If upgrading from 4.6 this is _VELZ_IMAX * 0.01.

params.name: Q_P_D_VEL_D
params.description: Velocity (vertical) controller D gain. Corrects short-term changes in velocity. Previously _VELZ_D.

params.name: Q_P_D_VEL_FF
params.description: Velocity (vertical) controller Feed Forward gain. Produces an output that is proportional to the magnitude of the target. Previously _VELZ_FF.

params.name: Q_P_D_VEL_FLTE
params.description: Velocity (vertical) error filter. This filter (in Hz) is applied to the input for P and I terms. Previously _VELZ_FLTE.

params.name: Q_P_D_VEL_FLTD
params.humanName: Velocity (vertical) input filter for D term
params.description: Velocity (vertical) input filter for D term. This filter (in Hz) is applied to the input for D terms. Previously _VELZ_FLTD.

params.name: Q_P_D_ACC_P
params.description: Acceleration (vertical) controller P gain. Converts the difference between desired vertical acceleration and actual acceleration into a motor output. If upgrading from 4.6 this is _ACCZ_P * 0.1.

params.name: Q_P_D_ACC_I
params.description: Acceleration (vertical) controller I gain. Corrects long-term difference in desired vertical acceleration and actual acceleration. If upgrading from 4.6 this is _ACCZ_I * 0.1.

params.name: Q_P_D_ACC_IMAX
params.description: Acceleration (vertical) controller I gain maximum. Constrains the maximum pwm that the I term will generate. If upgrading from 4.6 this is _ACCZ_IMAX * 0.001.

params.name: Q_P_D_ACC_D
params.description: Acceleration (vertical) controller D gain. Compensates for short-term change in desired vertical acceleration vs actual acceleration. If upgrading from 4.6 this is _ACCZ_D * 0.1.

params.name: Q_P_D_ACC_FF
params.description: Acceleration (vertical) controller feed forward. If upgrading from 4.6 this is _ACCZ_FF * 0.1.

params.name: Q_P_D_ACC_FLTT
params.humanName: Acceleration (vertical) controller target frequency in Hz
params.description: Acceleration (vertical) controller target frequency in Hz. Previously _ACCZ_FLTT.

params.name: Q_P_D_ACC_FLTE
params.humanName: Acceleration (vertical) controller error frequency in Hz
params.description: Acceleration (vertical) controller error frequency in Hz. Previously _ACCZ_FLTE.

params.name: Q_P_D_ACC_FLTD
params.humanName: Acceleration (vertical) controller derivative frequency in Hz
params.description: Acceleration (vertical) controller derivative frequency in Hz. Previously _ACCZ_FLTD.

params.name: Q_P_D_ACC_SMAX
params.description: Sets an upper limit on the slew rate produced by the combined P and D gains. If the amplitude of the control action produced by the rate feedback exceeds this value, then the D+P gain is reduced to respect the limit. This limits the amplitude of high frequency oscillations caused by an excessive gain. The limit should be set to no more than 25% of the actuators maximum slew rate to allow for load effects. Note: The gain will not be reduced to less than 10% of the nominal value. A value of zero will disable this feature.

params.name: Q_P_D_ACC_PDMX
params.description: Acceleration (vertical) controller PD sum maximum. The maximum/minimum value that the sum of the P and D term can output. If upgrading from 4.6 this is _ACCZ_P * 0.1.

params.name: Q_P_D_ACC_D_FF
params.description: FF D Gain which produces an output that is proportional to the rate of change of the target. If upgrading from 4.6 this is _ACCZ_P * 0.1.

params.name: Q_P_D_ACC_NTF
params.description: Accel (vertical) Target notch filter index. If upgrading from 4.6 this is Previously _ACCZ_NTF.

params.name: Q_P_D_ACC_NEF
params.description: Accel (vertical) Error notch filter index. If upgrading from 4.6 this is Previously _ACCZ_NEF.

params.name: Q_P_NE_VEL_P
params.description: Velocity (horizontal) P gain. Converts the difference between desired and actual velocity to a target acceleration. Previously _VELXY_P.

params.name: Q_P_NE_VEL_I
params.description: Velocity (horizontal) I gain. Corrects long-term difference between desired and actual velocity to a target acceleration. Previously _VELXY_I.

params.name: Q_P_NE_VEL_D
params.description: Velocity (horizontal) D gain. Corrects short-term changes in velocity. Previously _VELXY_D.

params.name: Q_P_NE_VEL_IMAX
params.description: Velocity (horizontal) integrator maximum. Constrains the target acceleration that the I gain will output. If upgrading from 4.6 this is _VELXY_IMAX * 0.01.

params.name: Q_P_NE_VEL_FLTE
params.description: Velocity (horizontal) input filter. This filter (in Hz) is applied to the input for P and I terms. Previously _VELXY_FLTE.

params.name: Q_P_NE_VEL_FLTD
params.description: Velocity (horizontal) input filter. This filter (in Hz) is applied to the input for D term. Previously _VELXY_FLTD.

params.name: Q_P_NE_VEL_FF
params.description: Velocity (horizontal) feed forward gain. Converts the difference between desired velocity to a target acceleration. Previously _VELXY_FF.

params.name: Q_TAILSIT_ENABLE
params.description: This enables Tailsitter functionality. A value of 2 forces Qassist active and always stabilize in forward flight with airmode for stabilisation at 0 throttle, for use on vehicles with no control surfaces, vehicle will not arm in forward flight modes, see also Q_OPTIONS "Mtrs_Only_Qassist"

params.name: Q_TAILSIT_ANGLE
params.description: This is the pitch angle at which tailsitter aircraft will change from VTOL control to fixed wing control.

params.name: Q_TAILSIT_ANG_VT
params.description: This is the pitch angle at which tailsitter aircraft will change from fixed wing control to VTOL control, if zero Q_TAILSIT_ANGLE will be used

params.name: Q_TAILSIT_INPUT
params.description: This controls whether stick input when hovering as a tailsitter follows the conventions for fixed wing hovering or multicopter hovering. When PlaneMode is not enabled (bit0 = 0) the roll stick will roll the aircraft in earth frame and yaw stick will yaw in earth frame. When PlaneMode input is enabled, the roll and yaw sticks are swapped so that the roll stick controls earth-frame yaw and rudder controls earth-frame roll. When body-frame roll is enabled (bit1 = 1), the yaw stick controls earth-frame yaw rate and the roll stick controls roll in the tailsitter's body frame when flying level.

params.name: Q_TAILSIT_VFGAIN
params.humanName: Tailsitter vector thrust gain in forward flight
params.description: This controls the amount of vectored thrust control used in forward flight for a vectored tailsitter

params.name: Q_TAILSIT_VHGAIN
params.humanName: Tailsitter vector thrust gain in hover
params.description: This controls the amount of vectored thrust control used in hover for a vectored tailsitter

params.name: Q_TAILSIT_VHPOW
params.description: This controls the amount of extra pitch given to the vectored control when at high pitch errors

params.name: Q_TAILSIT_GSCMAX
params.description: Maximum gain scaling for tailsitter Q_TAILSIT_GSCMSK options

params.name: Q_TAILSIT_RLL_MX
params.description: Maximum Allowed roll angle for tailsitters. If this is zero then Q_A_ANGLE_MAX is used.

params.name: Q_TAILSIT_MOTMX
params.description: Bitmask of motors to remain active in forward flight for a 'Copter' tailsitter. Non-zero indicates airframe is a Copter tailsitter and uses copter style motor layouts determined by Q_FRAME_CLASS and Q_FRAME_TYPE. This should be zero for non-Copter tailsitters.

params.name: Q_TAILSIT_GSCMSK
params.description: Bitmask of gain scaling methods to be applied: Throttle: scale gains with throttle, ATT_THR: reduce gain at high throttle/tilt, 2:Disk theory velocity calculation, requires Q_TAILSIT_DSKLD to be set, ATT_THR must not be set, 3:Altitude correction, scale with air density

params.name: Q_TAILSIT_GSCMIN
params.description: Minimum gain scaling for tailsitter Q_TAILSIT_GSCMSK options

params.name: Q_TAILSIT_DSKLD
params.description: This is the vehicle weight in kg divided by the total disk area of all propellers in m^2. Only used with Q_TAILSIT_GSCMSK = 4

params.name: Q_TAILSIT_RAT_FW
params.humanName: Tailsitter VTOL to forward flight transition rate
params.description: The pitch rate at which tailsitter aircraft will pitch down in the transition from VTOL to forward flight

params.name: Q_TAILSIT_RAT_VT
params.humanName: Tailsitter forward flight to VTOL transition rate
params.description: The pitch rate at which tailsitter aircraft will pitch up in the transition from forward flight to VTOL

params.name: Q_TAILSIT_THR_VT
params.humanName: Tailsitter forward flight to VTOL transition throttle
params.description: Throttle used during FW->VTOL transition, -1 uses hover throttle

params.name: Q_TAILSIT_VT_R_P
params.humanName: Tailsitter VTOL control surface roll gain
params.description: Scale from PID output to control surface, for use where a single axis is actuated by both motors and Tilt/control surface on a copter style tailsitter, increase to favor control surfaces and reduce motor output by reducing gains

params.name: Q_TAILSIT_VT_P_P
params.humanName: Tailsitter VTOL control surface pitch gain
params.description: Scale from PID output to control surface, for use where a single axis is actuated by both motors and Tilt/control surface on a copter style tailsitter, increase to favor control surfaces and reduce motor output by reducing gains

params.name: Q_TAILSIT_VT_Y_P
params.humanName: Tailsitter VTOL control surface yaw gain
params.description: Scale from PID output to control surface, for use where a single axis is actuated by both motors and Tilt/control surface on a copter style tailsitter, increase to favor control surfaces and reduce motor output by reducing gains

params.name: Q_TAILSIT_MIN_VO
params.humanName: Tailsitter Disk loading minimum outflow speed
params.description: Use in conjunction with disk theory gain scaling and Q_TAILSIT_DSKLD to specify minimum airspeed over control surfaces, this will be used to boost throttle, when descending for example, 0 disables

params.name: Q_TILT_ENABLE
params.description: This enables Tiltrotor functionality

params.name: Q_TILT_MASK
params.description: This is a bitmask of motors that are tiltable in a tiltrotor (or tiltwing). The mask is in terms of the standard motor order for the frame type.

params.name: Q_TILT_RATE_UP
params.description: This is the maximum speed at which the motor angle will change for a tiltrotor when moving from forward flight to hover

params.name: Q_TILT_MAX
params.description: This is the maximum angle of the tiltable motors at which multicopter control will be enabled. Beyond this angle the plane will fly solely as a fixed wing aircraft and the motors will tilt to their maximum angle at the TILT_RATE

params.name: Q_TILT_TYPE
params.description: This is the type of tiltrotor when TILT_MASK is non-zero. A continuous tiltrotor can tilt the rotors to any angle on demand. A binary tiltrotor assumes a retract style servo where the servo is either fully forward or fully up. In both cases the servo can't move faster than Q_TILT_RATE. A vectored yaw tiltrotor will use the tilt of the motors to control yaw in hover, Bicopter tiltrotor must use the tailsitter frame class (10)

params.name: Q_TILT_RATE_DN
params.description: This is the maximum speed at which the motor angle will change for a tiltrotor when moving from hover to forward flight. When this is zero the Q_TILT_RATE_UP value is used.

params.name: Q_TILT_YAW_ANGLE
params.humanName: Tilt minimum angle for vectored yaw
params.description: This is the angle of the tilt servos when in VTOL mode and at minimum output (fully back). This needs to be set in addition to Q_TILT_TYPE=2, to enable vectored control for yaw in tilt quadplanes. This is also used to limit the forward travel of bicopter tilts(Q_TILT_TYPE=3) when in VTOL modes.

params.name: Q_TILT_FIX_ANGLE
params.description: This is the angle the motors tilt down when at maximum output for forward flight. Set this to a non-zero value to enable vectoring for roll/pitch in forward flight on tilt-vectored aircraft

params.name: Q_TILT_FIX_GAIN
params.description: This is the gain for use of tilting motors in fixed wing flight for tilt vectored quadplanes

params.name: Q_TILT_WING_FLAP
params.humanName: Tiltrotor tilt angle that will be used as flap
params.description: For use on tilt wings, the wing will tilt up to this angle for flap, transition will be complete when the wing reaches this angle from the forward fight position, 0 disables

params.name: Q_WP_RFND_USE
params.humanName: Waypoint missions use rangefinder for terrain following
params.description: This controls if waypoint missions use rangefinder for terrain following

params.name: Q_WP_JERK
params.description: Defines the horizontal jerk in m/s/s used during missions

params.name: Q_WP_TER_MARGIN
params.description: Waypoint Terrain following altitude margin.  Vehicle will stop if distance from target altitude is larger than this margin (in meters)

params.name: Q_WP_SPD
params.description: Speed in m/s which the aircraft will attempt to maintain horizontally during a WP mission

params.name: Q_WP_RADIUS_M
params.description: Distance from a waypoint, that when crossed indicates the wp has been reached.

params.name: Q_WP_SPD_UP
params.description: Speed in m/s which the aircraft will attempt to maintain while climbing during a WP mission

params.name: Q_WP_SPD_DN
params.description: Speed in m/s which the aircraft will attempt to maintain while descending during a WP mission

params.name: Q_WP_ACC
params.description: Horizontal acceleration in m/s/s used during missions

params.name: Q_WP_ACC_Z
params.description: Vertical acceleration in m/s/s used during missions

params.name: Q_WP_ACC_CNR
params.description: Maximum cornering acceleration in m/s/s used during missions.  If zero uses 2x accel value.

params.name: Q_WVANE_ENABLE
params.description: Enable weather vaning.  When active, the aircraft will automatically yaw into wind when in a VTOL position controlled mode. Pilot yaw commands override the weathervaning action.

values.label: Only use during takeoffs or landing see weathervane takeoff and land override parameters

params.name: Q_WVANE_GAIN
params.description: This converts the target roll/pitch angle of the aircraft into the correcting (into wind) yaw rate. e.g. Gain = 2, roll = 30 deg, pitch = 0 deg, yaw rate = 60 deg/s.

params.name: Q_WVANE_ANG_MIN
params.description: The minimum target roll/pitch angle before active weathervaning will start.  This provides a dead zone that is particularly useful for poorly trimmed quadplanes.

params.name: Q_WVANE_HGT_MIN
params.description: Above this height weathervaning is permitted.  If RNGFND_LANDING is enabled or terrain is enabled then this parameter sets height AGL. Otherwise this parameter sets height above home.  Set zero to ignore minimum height requirement to activate weathervaning

params.name: Q_WVANE_SPD_MAX
params.description: Below this ground speed weathervaning is permitted. Set to 0 to ignore this condition when checking if vehicle should weathervane.

params.name: Q_WVANE_VELZ_MAX
params.description: The maximum climb or descent speed that the vehicle will still attempt to weathervane. Set to 0 to ignore this condition to get the aircraft to weathervane at any climb/descent rate.  This is particularly useful for aircraft with low disc loading that struggle with yaw control in decent.

params.name: Q_WVANE_TAKEOFF
params.description: Override the weather vaning behaviour when in takeoffs

params.name: Q_WVANE_LAND
params.description: Override the weather vaning behaviour when in landing

params.name: Q_WVANE_OPTIONS
params.description: Options impacting weathervaning behaviour

bitmask.label: Use pitch when nose or tail-in for faster weathervaning

params.name: RALLY_TOTAL
params.description: Number of rally points currently loaded

params.name: RALLY_LIMIT_KM
params.description: Maximum distance to rally point. If the closest rally point is more than this number of kilometers from the current position and the home location is closer than any of the rally points from the current position then do RTL to home rather than to the closest rally point. This prevents a leftover rally point from a different airfield being used accidentally. If this is set to 0 then the closest rally point is always used.

params.name: RALLY_INCL_HOME
params.description: Controls if Home is included as a Rally point (i.e. as a safe landing place) for RTL

params.name: RC_OVERRIDE_TIME
params.description: Timeout after which RC overrides will no longer be used, and RC input will resume, 0 will disable RC overrides, -1 will never timeout, and continue using overrides until they are disabled

params.name: RC_OPTIONS
params.description: RC input options

bitmask.label: Ignore Receiver Failsafe bit but allow other RC failsafes if setup
Skip the arming check for neutral Roll/Pitch/Yaw sticks
Suppress CRSF mode/rate message for ELRS systems
Use Link Quality for RSSI with CRSF
Annotate CRSF flight mode with * on disarm
Clear MAVLink overrides on any stick input

params.name: RC_PROTOCOLS
params.description: Bitmask of enabled RC protocols. Allows narrowing the protocol detection to only specific types of RC receivers which can avoid issues with incorrect detection. Set to 1 to enable all protocols.

params.name: RC_FS_TIMEOUT
params.description: RC failsafe will trigger this many seconds after loss of RC

params.name: RCMAP_ROLL
params.description: Roll channel number. This is useful when you have a RC transmitter that can't change the channel order easily. Roll is normally on channel 1, but you can move it to any channel with this parameter.  Reboot is required for changes to take effect.

params.name: RCMAP_PITCH
params.description: Pitch channel number. This is useful when you have a RC transmitter that can't change the channel order easily. Pitch is normally on channel 2, but you can move it to any channel with this parameter.  Reboot is required for changes to take effect.

params.name: RCMAP_THROTTLE
params.description: Throttle channel number. This is useful when you have a RC transmitter that can't change the channel order easily. Throttle is normally on channel 3, but you can move it to any channel with this parameter. Reboot is required for changes to take effect.

params.name: RCMAP_YAW
params.description: Yaw channel number. This is useful when you have a RC transmitter that can't change the channel order easily. Yaw (also known as rudder) is normally on channel 4, but you can move it to any channel with this parameter.  Reboot is required for changes to take effect.

params.name: RLL2SRV_TCONST
params.description: Time constant in seconds from demanded to achieved roll angle. Most models respond well to 0.5. May be reduced for faster responses, but setting lower than a model can achieve will not help.

params.name: RLL2SRV_RMAX
params.description: This sets the maximum roll rate that the attitude controller will demand (degrees/sec) in angle stabilized modes. Setting it to zero disables this limit.

params.name: RLL_RATE_P
params.humanName: Roll axis rate controller P gain
params.description: Roll axis rate controller P gain. Corrects in proportion to the difference between the desired roll rate vs actual roll rate

params.name: RLL_RATE_I
params.humanName: Roll axis rate controller I gain
params.description: Roll axis rate controller I gain.  Corrects long-term difference in desired roll rate vs actual roll rate

params.name: RLL_RATE_IMAX
params.humanName: Roll axis rate controller I gain maximum
params.description: Roll axis rate controller I gain maximum.  Constrains the maximum that the I term will output

params.name: RLL_RATE_D
params.humanName: Roll axis rate controller D gain
params.description: Roll axis rate controller D gain.  Compensates for short-term change in desired roll rate vs actual roll rate

params.name: RLL_RATE_FF
params.humanName: Roll axis rate controller feed forward
params.description: Roll axis rate controller feed forward

params.name: RLL_RATE_FLTT
params.humanName: Roll axis rate controller target frequency in Hz
params.description: Roll axis rate controller target frequency in Hz

params.name: RLL_RATE_FLTE
params.humanName: Roll axis rate controller error frequency in Hz
params.description: Roll axis rate controller error frequency in Hz

params.name: RLL_RATE_FLTD
params.humanName: Roll axis rate controller derivative frequency in Hz
params.description: Roll axis rate controller derivative frequency in Hz

params.name: RLL_RATE_SMAX
params.description: Sets an upper limit on the slew rate produced by the combined P and D gains. If the amplitude of the control action produced by the rate feedback exceeds this value, then the D+P gain is reduced to respect the limit. This limits the amplitude of high frequency oscillations caused by an excessive gain. The limit should be set to no more than 25% of the actuators maximum slew rate to allow for load effects. Note: The gain will not be reduced to less than 10% of the nominal value. A value of zero will disable this feature.

params.name: RLL_RATE_PDMX
params.humanName: Roll axis rate controller PD sum maximum
params.description: Roll axis rate controller PD sum maximum.  The maximum/minimum value that the sum of the P and D term can output

params.name: RLL_RATE_D_FF
params.description: FF D Gain which produces an output that is proportional to the rate of change of the target

params.name: RLL_RATE_NTF
params.description: Roll Target notch filter index

params.name: RLL_RATE_NEF
params.description: Roll Error notch filter index

params.name: RLL2SRV_ACCEL
params.description: Roll acceleration limit. Setting to zero disables input shaping.

params.name: RLL_ANGLE_P
params.description: Roll angle P gain. If zero a gain of (1 / RLL2SRV_TCONST) will be used.

params.name: RNGFND1_TYPE
params.description: Type of connected rangefinder

params.name: RNGFND1_PIN
params.description: Analog or PWM input pin that rangefinder is connected to. Analog RSSI or Airspeed ports can be used for Analog inputs (some autopilots provide others also), Non-IOMCU Servo/MotorOutputs can be used for PWM input when configured as "GPIOs". Values for some autopilots are given as examples. Search wiki for "Analog pins" for analog pin or "GPIOs", if PWM input type, to determine pin number.

params.name: RNGFND1_SCALING
params.description: Scaling factor between rangefinder reading and distance. For the linear and inverted functions this is in meters per volt. For the hyperbolic function the units are meterVolts. For Maxbotix serial sonar this is unit conversion to meters.

params.name: RNGFND1_OFFSET
params.description: Offset in volts for zero distance for analog rangefinders. Offset added to distance in centimeters for PWM lidars

params.name: RNGFND1_FUNCTION
params.description: Control over what function is used to calculate distance. For a linear function, the distance is (voltage-offset)*scaling. For a inverted function the distance is (offset-voltage)*scaling. For a hyperbolic function the distance is scaling/(voltage-offset). The functions return the distance in meters.

params.name: RNGFND1_MIN
params.description: Minimum distance in metres that rangefinder can reliably read

params.name: RNGFND1_MAX
params.description: Maximum distance in metres that rangefinder can reliably read

params.name: RNGFND1_STOP_PIN
params.description: Digital pin that enables/disables rangefinder measurement for the pwm rangefinder. A value of -1 means no pin. If this is set, then the pin is set to 1 to enable the rangefinder and set to 0 to disable it. This is used to enable powersaving when out of range. Some common values are given, but see the Wiki's "GPIOs" page for how to determine the pin number for a given autopilot.

params.name: RNGFND1_RMETRIC
params.description: This parameter sets whether an analog rangefinder is ratiometric. Most analog rangefinders are ratiometric, meaning that their output voltage is influenced by the supply voltage. Some analog rangefinders (such as the SF/02) have their own internal voltage regulators so they are not ratiometric.

params.name: RNGFND1_PWRRNG
params.description: This parameter sets the estimated terrain distance in meters above which the sensor will be put into a power saving mode (if available). A value of zero means power saving is not enabled

params.name: RNGFND1_GNDCLR
params.humanName: Distance from the range finder to the ground
params.description: This parameter sets the expected range measurement that the range finder should return when the vehicle is on the ground.

params.name: RNGFND1_ADDR
params.description: This sets the bus address of the sensor, where applicable. Used for the I2C and DroneCAN sensors to allow for multiple sensors on different addresses.

params.name: RNGFND1_POS_X
params.description: X position of the rangefinder in body frame. Positive X is forward of the origin. Use the zero range datum point if supplied.

params.name: RNGFND1_POS_Y
params.description: Y position of the rangefinder in body frame. Positive Y is to the right of the origin. Use the zero range datum point if supplied.

params.name: RNGFND1_POS_Z
params.description: Z position of the rangefinder in body frame. Positive Z is down from the origin. Use the zero range datum point if supplied.

params.name: RNGFND1_ORIENT
params.description: Orientation of rangefinder

params.name: RNGFND1_WSP_MAVG
params.description: Sets the number of historic range results to use for calculating the current range result. When MAVG is greater than 1, the current range result will be the current measured value averaged with the N-1 previous results

params.name: RNGFND1_WSP_MEDF
params.description: Sets the window size for the real-time median filter. When MEDF is greater than 0 the median filter is active

params.name: RNGFND1_WSP_FRQ
params.description: Sets the repetition frequency of the ranging operation in Hertz. Upon entering the desired frequency the system will calculate the nearest frequency that it can handle according to the resolution of internal timers.

params.name: RNGFND1_WSP_AVG
params.description: Sets the number of pulses to be used in multi-pulse averaging mode. In this mode, a sequence of rapid fire ranges are taken and then averaged to improve the accuracy of the measurement

params.name: RNGFND1_WSP_THR
params.description: Sets the system sensitivity. Larger values of THR represent higher sensitivity. The system may limit the maximum value of THR to prevent excessive false alarm rates based on settings made at the factory. Set to -1 for automatic threshold adjustments

params.name: RNGFND1_WSP_BAUD
params.description: Desired baud rate

params.name: RNGFND1_RECV_ID
params.description: The receive ID of the CAN frames. A value of zero means all IDs are accepted.

params.name: RNGFND1_SNR_MIN
params.description: RangeFinder Minimum signal strength (SNR) to accept distance

params.name: RNGFND1_GRF_RET
params.description: Selects which single return to use.

params.name: RNGFND1_GRF_ST
params.description: Minimum acceptable return signal strength in dB. Returns weaker than this will be ignored. Set to 0 to disable filtering.

params.name: RNGFND1_GRF_RATE
params.description: The update rate of the sensor in Hz.

For a inverted function the distance is (offset-voltage)*scaling. For a hyperbolic function the distance is scaling/(voltage-offset). The functions return the distance in meters.

params.name: RNGFND8_MIN
params.description: Minimum distance in metres that rangefinder can reliably read

params.name: RNGFND8_MAX
params.description: Maximum distance in metres that rangefinder can reliably read

params.name: RNGFND8_STOP_PIN
params.description: Digital pin that enables/disables rangefinder measurement for the pwm rangefinder. A value of -1 means no pin. If this is set, then the pin is set to 1 to enable the rangefinder and set to 0 to disable it. This is used to enable powersaving when out of range. Some common values are given, but see the Wiki's "GPIOs" page for how to determine the pin number for a given autopilot.

params.name: RNGFND8_RMETRIC
params.description: This parameter sets whether an analog rangefinder is ratiometric. Most analog rangefinders are ratiometric, meaning that their output voltage is influenced by the supply voltage. Some analog rangefinders (such as the SF/02) have their own internal voltage regulators so they are not ratiometric.

params.name: RNGFND8_PWRRNG

params.name: RNGFND8_GNDCLR

params.name: RNGFND8_POS_Y

params.name: RNGFND8_ORIENT
params.description: Orientation of rangefinder

params.name: RNGFND8_WSP_MAVG
params.description: Sets the number of historic range results to use for calculating the current range result. When MAVG is greater than 1, the current range result will be the current measured value averaged with the N-1 previous results

params.name: RNGFND8_WSP_MEDF
params.description: Sets the window size for the real-time median filter. When MEDF is greater than 0 the median filter is active

params.name: RNGFND8_WSP_FRQ
params.description: Sets the repetition frequency of the ranging operation in Hertz. Upon entering the desired frequency the system will calculate the nearest frequency that it can handle according to the resolution of internal timers.

params.name: RNGFND8_WSP_AVG
params.description: Sets the number of pulses to be used in multi-pulse averaging mode. In this mode, a sequence of rapid fire ranges are taken and then averaged to improve the accuracy of the measurement

params.name: RNGFND8_WSP_THR
params.description: Sets the system sensitivity. Larger values of THR represent higher sensitivity. The system may limit the maximum value of THR to prevent excessive false alarm rates based on settings made at the factory. Set to -1 for automatic threshold adjustments

Values for some autopilots are given as examples. Search wiki for "Analog pins" for analog pin or "GPIOs", if PWM input type, to determine pin number.

params.name: RSSI_PIN_LOW
params.description: RSSI pin's voltage received on the RSSI_ANA_PIN when the signal strength is the weakest. Some radio receivers put out inverted values so this value may be higher than RSSI_PIN_HIGH. When using pin 103, the maximum value of the parameter is 3.3V.

params.name: RSSI_PIN_HIGH
params.description: RSSI pin's voltage received on the RSSI_ANA_PIN when the signal strength is the strongest. Some radio receivers put out inverted values so this value may be lower than RSSI_PIN_LOW. When using pin 103, the maximum value of the parameter is 3.3V.

params.name: RSSI_CHANNEL
params.description: The channel number where RSSI will be output by the radio receiver (5 and above).

params.name: RSSI_CHAN_LOW
params.description: PWM value that the radio receiver will put on the RSSI_CHANNEL or RSSI_ANA_PIN when the signal strength is the weakest. Some radio receivers output inverted values so this value may be lower than RSSI_CHAN_HIGH

params.name: RSSI_CHAN_HIGH
params.description: PWM value that the radio receiver will put on the RSSI_CHANNEL or RSSI_ANA_PIN when the signal strength is the strongest. Some radio receivers output inverted values so this value may be higher than RSSI_CHAN_LOW

params.name: SCR_THD_PRIORITY
params.description: This sets the priority of the scripting thread. This is normally set to a low priority to prevent scripts from interfering with other parts of the system. Advanced users can change this priority if scripting needs to be prioritised for realtime applications. WARNING: changing this parameter can impact the stability of your flight controller. The scipting thread priority in this parameter is chosen based on a set of system level priorities for other subsystems. It is strongly recommended that you use the lowest priority that is sufficient for your application. Note that all scripts run at the same priority, so if you raise this priority you must carefully audit all lua scripts for behaviour that does not interfere with the operation of the system.

The HalfDuplex option controls half-duplex (onewire) mode, where both transmit and receive is done on the transmit wire. The Swap option allows the RX and TX pins to be swapped on STM32F7 based boards.  NOTE that two bits have moved from this parameter into MAVn_OPTIONS!

bitmask.label: Don't forward mavlink to/from (moved to MAVn_OPTIONS >4.7)

params.name: SERIAL_PASS1
params.description: This sets one side of pass-through between two serial ports. Once both sides are set then all data received on either port will be passed to the other port

params.name: SERIAL_PASS2
params.description: This sets one side of pass-through between two serial ports. Once both sides are set then all data received on either port will be passed to the other port. This parameter is normally reset to -1 on reboot, disabling passthrough. If SERIAL_PASSTIMO is set to -1 then it is not reset on reboot.

params.name: SERIAL_PASSTIMO
params.description: This sets a timeout for serial pass-through in seconds. When the pass-through is enabled by setting the SERIAL_PASS1 and SERIAL_PASS2 parameters then it remains in effect until no data comes from the first port for SERIAL_PASSTIMO seconds. This allows the port to revent to its normal usage (such as MAVLink connection to a GCS) when it is no longer needed. A value of 0 means no timeout. A value of -1 means no timeout and the SERIAL_PASS2 parameter is not reset on reboot.

params.name: SERIAL7_PROTOCOL
params.description: Control what protocol Serial7 port should be used for. Note that the Frsky options require external converter hardware. See the wiki for details.

params.name: SERIAL7_BAUD
params.description: The baud rate used for Serial7. Most stm32-based boards can support rates of up to 1500. If you setup a rate you cannot support and then can't connect to your board you should load a firmware from a different vehicle type. That will reset all your parameters to defaults.
